title: Persistent Memory Injection (MemoryBot)
summary: As documented, an attacker plants instructions that activate in later sessions for other users. As implemented, the planted text is stored and shown to any later caller.

LC.rationale: The attacker's natural-language chat message reaches MemoryBot's shared memory store unsanitized and is later surfaced to callers, with no transformation or validation before the sink.

CP.rationale: The planted text is stored in a shared in-process list (up to 50 entries) that survives the originating request and is reachable by any later caller, satisfying cross-session persistence within the server process.
evidence_refs: MemoryBot keeps up to 50 flagged messages in one in-process list shared by every caller. The list survives across requests and callers and is lost when the process stops. Recall prints the entries.

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to MemoryBot's own memory list and its recall replies; no other agent, principal, or trust boundary is crossed.

RH.rationale: No evaluator, verifier, or reward channel exists on MemoryBot's path; the handlers are deterministic regex-matched replies with no proxy objective to satisfy.
evidence_refs: In the default configuration no model is called. Chat agents are deterministic handlers that match regular expressions and return scripted replies.
No handler changes later replies because of a stored entry.

ES.rationale: MemoryBot's declared tools (read_file, write_file, search) are fixed scripted handlers, and the memory path is a hard-coded in-process list; no dynamic or unvetted extension binding is reachable.
evidence_refs: Chat agents list tool names in their definitions, but only the scripted paths above execute anything.

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. As documented, MemoryBot treats stored instructions as standing directives it follows in later conversations, which is model-directed goal pursuit, but it takes no multi-step action sequence.
